sections.h2: Roof age in Ocotillo depends on the neighborhood
sections.body:
Ocotillo isn't one subdivision. It's a master-planned community of about 40 separate neighborhoods, and they weren't all built at once. Most homes went up in the 1990s and 2000s, building continued into the 2010s, and a few homes were completed in the 2020s.

That spread matters for your roof. A home in the Estates at Ocotillo built in 1996 has a roof that's roughly 30 years old, while the Villas at Villa Del Lago, which Standard Pacific Homes opened in 2015, are only about a decade in. Two homes a mile apart can need completely different work, so we begin every Ocotillo visit by confirming when the house was built and whether the roof has ever been redone.

sections.h2: What the original 1990s roofs usually need now
sections.body:
Pitched roofs from that era in the Chandler area were commonly finished with concrete tile over felt underlayment. The tile can last for decades, but felt underlayment under the Arizona sun usually wears out in about 20–25 years. For any roof in Ocotillo's earliest neighborhoods that is still original, that window has already closed.

When underlayment fails, water that slips past the tile no longer drains off cleanly. Early signs are easy to miss: a faint ceiling stain near an outside wall, a musty attic, or dark spots on the roof deck. The usual fix is a tile underlayment replacement, where we lift the tile, install new underlayment and flashing, and relay the sound tile.

Ocotillo mixes detached houses with townhomes, patio homes and condos. On attached homes, one roof often runs across several units, so a leak above your neighbor's garage can be the same problem that's staining your ceiling.

Who pays for and schedules roof work on attached homes varies by association, and we don't have those rules for each Ocotillo neighborhood. Check your own HOA documents first. If the roof is your responsibility, we can inspect it and explain what we find in a way you can share with the neighbors who share it.

The community is built around interconnected man-made lakes filled with reclaimed water from a City of Chandler treatment plant, plus the 27-hole Ocotillo Golf Club, which Ted Robinson designed in 1986. Plenty of homes back onto water or fairways.

Homes along a golf course can collect cracked or chipped tiles from stray balls. A single broken tile seems minor, but it exposes the underlayment beneath it to direct sun and rain. If you hear a thump on the roof or spot tile fragments in the yard, have the area checked before monsoon season.

Arizona's monsoon season runs June 15–September 30, and the strongest storms bring wind gusts, sideways rain and blowing debris. On tile roofs, the common damage is slipped or broken tiles along ridges and edges, and lifted flashing around walls and vents. Our roof inspections page explains what a post-storm check covers.
bullets: Walk the yard after a big storm and look for tile pieces on the ground.
Check ceilings and the tops of exterior walls for new stains.
Clear leaves and debris from valleys and roof-to-wall corners in late spring.
Schedule an inspection if anything looks out of place rather than waiting for a leak.

Listings in Paseo Trail show Cresleigh Homes houses built in 2003 with tile roofs. At around 23 years old, an original roof here is past the early part of the 20–25 year range when felt underlayment typically wears out under Arizona tile.

Many roofs this age still don't leak. But the underlayment is aging every summer, and it's easier to plan the work on your schedule than to wait for a monsoon storm to find the weak spot.

sections.h2: How we evaluate a 23-year-old tile roof
sections.body:
On a roof this age, we're answering one main question: how much life does the underlayment have left? We check tile for cracks and slipping, look at flashing at walls and valleys, inspect pipe boots and vents, and lift tiles in a few places to see the underlayment directly.

From there, the recommendation is usually one of three things: small repairs now, a lift and relay soon, or a full replacement if the tile itself is in poor shape. Learn more about our roof inspections.

sections.h2: Easy things owners can watch for
bullets: Pieces of tile in flower beds or on the patio
Stains or bubbling paint on ceilings, especially near outside walls
Water marks on the underside of the roof deck in the attic
Tiles that look out of line from the street
Leaves and debris piling up in valleys
sections.body: You don't need to climb a ladder to keep tabs on your roof. Most early warnings are visible from the ground or the attic hatch.

sections.h2: Heat, UV and the south-facing slope
sections.body: In Chandler, long summers of triple-digit heat and intense UV are what age underlayment. The slopes that face south and west take the most sun, so those sections often show wear before the rest of the roof. If we find a problem on one side, we'll check whether the opposite slopes are in better shape, which can affect what we recommend.

Paseo Trail has an HOA. If you plan to change the color or style of your tile, ask the association about approval first. A re-felt that reuses your tile keeps the roof looking the same. For cost factors, see our Roofing Cost Guide; every roof is different, and we give a written estimate after an inspection.

sections.h2: Shingle roofs in the Arizona sun
sections.body:
Asphalt shingles generally don't last as long as tile in the Valley. Intense UV and summer heat dry out the asphalt, granules wash off, and shingles curl, crack or blow off in monsoon winds. An original 1980s shingle roof would be far past its expected life, so a shingle roof on a Twelve Oaks home today has most likely been replaced at some point, though we can't say when for any particular house.

If your shingle roof is showing its age, look for:
bullets: Curled, cupped or cracked shingles
Bare spots where granules have worn away
Granules collecting in gutters or at downspouts
Missing shingles after a windy storm
Soft spots when walking near the edges, which can mean damaged decking

sections.h2: Replacing shingles: same material or switch?
sections.body:
When a shingle roof wears out, you can replace it with new asphalt shingles or consider switching to tile. Shingles cost less up front. Tile is heavier and lasts longer, but a house originally framed for shingles may need an engineering review before carrying tile weight.

Any change in roofing material would also likely need HOA approval. We can walk through the trade-offs with you during an estimate, and our roof types page compares the options.

A lift and relay replaces the underlayment and reuses sound tile; see our tile roofs page.

Twelve Oaks is made up of smaller single-family homes. Smaller footprints often mean simpler roof shapes with fewer valleys and transitions, which can make repairs and replacements more straightforward. We'll still inspect the whole roof, including flashing at walls and any patio covers, before recommending anything.

The Twelve Oaks HOA includes grounds maintenance. That doesn't tell us whether the association handles roofs, so check your HOA documents to confirm who is responsible for roof repairs and replacement before scheduling work. If a project changes the roof's look, ask about approval too.
